channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: London deletes posts praising Nigeria-US security partnership
item.description: The American strategist had called Nigeria Washington’s greatest ally in Africa and said the cooperation could widen economic and trade opportunities.

item.title: Sierra Leone analysis says vice presidency offers no clear path to succession
item.description: Political economist Foday M. Daboh argues that the office has not helped any vice president win the presidency, citing Solomon Berewa’s 2007 defeat.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burners cut economic trees as demand grows
item.description: Environmental Protection Agency official Paul Lamin says the trade leaves land exposed and threatens food security, while 65-year-old Pa Alimamy depends on it for his family’s.

item.title: Finance minister’s defender rejects call for his dismissal
item.description: Writer Foday M. Daboh says Sierra Leone’s economic hardship reflects global shocks, while arguing that Sheku Bangura restrained borrowing and inflation.

item.title: South Sudan Supreme Court directs Ajing to seek release from prosecutor
item.description: The court said it cannot order temporary release while the former presidential office director’s criminal case remains under investigation.

item.title: Namibia sets N$18 hourly minimum for security guards from January 2027
item.description: The final stage of a three-year wage transition will lift the minimum from N$16 and cover more than 30 000 workers nationwide.

item.title: Dehima Mission holds peace prayer in Tiassalé
item.description: The ceremony on 15 November formed part of the 31st annual peace celebrations organised by the AD3T association in the town.

item.title: Niger and Algeria advance technical work on trans-Saharan gas pipeline
item.description: An Algerian delegation is in Niamey from 17 to 20 November to settle route studies and operational steps for the Nigeria-to-Algeria project.

item.title: Russian House chief Dimitri Sytyi claims ignorance of Ndassima gold revenue
item.description: Sytyi said on Radio Ndeke Luka on 22 September 2026 that mercenary presence in the Central African Republic was free of charge.

item.title: Jonglei plans to move 135 Akobo exam candidates to Bor
item.description: The state says it will cover food and accommodation, but opposition officials and parents are still deciding whether to accept the plan.

item.title: Juba council sets 10 million SSP fine for selling alcohol to minors
item.description: The order also fines bars and shops for mixing alcohol with food and took effect on Monday after the caretaker mayor signed it.

item.title: Tunisia advances Grand Tunis mobility plan toward 2040
item.description: The study covers four governorates and will assess transport scenarios before officials select a plan for the region.

item.title: MRC asks Cameroon officials to clear election-candidate paperwork
item.description: The opposition party says thousands of its members face delays, refusals or demands for payment as they prepare for the 7 February 2027 vote.

item.title: FAM appoints Randy Waldrum as Scorchers coach
item.description: The American replaces Lovemore Fazili, whose tenure ends after he guided Malawi’s women to historic achievements.

item.title: IPCC recommends criminal charges against four Mauritius police officers
item.description: The commission sent its completed investigation into Élodie Thomas’s October shooting to the director of public prosecutions on 17 November.

item.title: Tunisia advances North African drug-regulation coordination in Cairo
item.description: At the committee’s second meeting, Tunisia and regional partners reviewed work on inspections and agreed on strategic documents for harmonising medicine procedures.

item.title: DP World plans to raise Mozambique cargo capacity to 650 mil TEU
item.description: The company told President Daniel Chapo it wants to lift handling capacity from 225 mil to approximately 650 mil TEU by the second quarter of 2027.

item.title: Police investigate assault on 22-year-old guard at Roches-Noires charcoal factory
item.description: The guard was found critically injured at his workplace on 16 November after an apparent dispute over a motorcycle engine, police were told.

item.title: OPay names five finalists for ₦18m National Innovation Challenge
item.description: The Nigerian digital bank says more than 11,000 students took part in selection, training and mentorship for the 2026 competition.

item.title: Ivory Coast says African energy bank will start on Jan. 2 in Abuja
item.description: Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly said the APPO and Afreximbank project will mobilise funding for Africa’s energy sector and infrastructure.

item.title: Congo loses to Comoros as Claude Le Roy announces resignation
item.description: The 1-0 defeat in Brazzaville leaves the national team last in Group G with two points after four matches in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

item.title: African Union education centre reviews girls’ schooling in N’Djamena
item.description: The delegation examined school re-entry measures, programmes for girls out of school and the results of the #AfricaEducatesHer campaign during a 11-13 November mission.

item.title: Senegal police arrest man accused of 19.2 million CFA job scam
item.description: Investigators allege the suspect took the money by promising a director's post at the Port autonome de Dakar at 2.5 million CFA francs a month.

item.title: UN Women brings private sector into Ebola response in Kinshasa
item.description: The workshop, held on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, brought together Congo's health ministry, UN Global Compact RDC and the OCDD.

item.title: Ghana and US renew cooperation to curb mercury pollution from illegal mining
item.description: The partnership will share scientific expertise and technology to improve monitoring and promote mercury-free gold extraction in Ghana.

item.title: Port-Louis waterfront festival returns with more than 30 food stalls
item.description: The 20-22 November event caps dish prices at Rs 275 and adds nightly concerts, DJ sets and radio activities.

item.title: Gobotswang challenges PEEPA-led Land Board recruitment in court
item.description: The Tswapong South MP says the process lacks legal authority over tribal land administration.

item.title: Amnesty urges war-crimes inquiry into RSF drone strikes in El Obeid
item.description: The rights group says nine attacks killed 37 civilians and injured 10 between June and August 2026, hitting homes and civilian infrastructure.

item.title: Mali road agency reports 2 deaths and 33 serious injuries daily
item.description: ANASER director Ousmane Bah Maïga cited the daily toll at a Bamako training session for 60 journalists on the new road code.

item.title: Bunyakiri faces harder access to care amid cholera and malaria
item.description: Fighting between the FRN and the army has worsened insecurity in the South Kivu health zone as cholera spreads and malaria cases peak.

item.title: Ghana banks face pressure to make digital services work reliably
item.description: The Bank of Ghana reported rising mobile-money transaction values and volumes in the first quarter of 2025 compared with a year earlier.

item.title: Congolese youth urged to take a bigger role in peacebuilding
item.description: At a Kinshasa conference, organisers asked young people to prevent conflict, back social cohesion and carry their pledges into their communities.

item.title: Gondwana shares begin trading on Namibia’s OTC market at N$9.60
item.description: The tourism group’s shares are available through four stockbrokers, but its OTC quotation does not raise new capital and trades can be infrequent.

item.title: Ghana Tourism Society sets three-day youth festival at Legon
item.description: The November 19-21 event will combine tourism education, a fair and cultural performances as the society marks its 20th anniversary.

item.title: BIDPA says Botswana budget is only moderately geared toward jobs
item.description: The policy institute says lasting employment depends on private-sector hiring, while unemployment stands at 27.6 per cent.

item.title: Telecom Namibia reports equipment thefts at northern sites
item.description: The break-ins damaged infrastructure at sites in Oshakati, Ongwediva and Ondangwa, disrupting voice and data services, the company said.

item.title: NBC launches campaign with TSh 4 million grand prizes for digital payments
item.description: The three-month programme runs through February 16, 2027, and includes rewards for customers and 150 merchant cashiers.

item.title: Liberia schedules maritime security dialogue in Margibi County
item.description: The Liberia Maritime Authority will convene officials and shipping leaders on Thursday, before the country assumes the UN Security Council presidency in December.

item.title: Liberian clinician urges response to estimated 56,000 HIV cases
item.description: Patience Lincoln says weak coordination and breaches of patient confidentiality are undermining prevention and treatment across Liberia.

item.title: Drone strikes drive most civilian deaths in Sudan, UN rights office finds
item.description: The UN Human Rights Office counted more than 2,230 civilians killed in Sudan from January to October, with over 1,630 of those deaths caused by drones.

item.title: White Nile sets diesel at SDG 69,842.50 a gallon as farmers report shortages
item.description: The state also priced petrol at SDG 53,365 a gallon, while farmers say scarce diesel is disrupting irrigation in Um Rimta.

item.title: Emmanuel Christian University graduates 131 in Yei
item.description: The graduates included 60 from Business Administration, 47 from Education and 24 from Theology at the university’s 18th ceremony.

item.title: Tunisia launches €60 million green finance programme for small businesses
item.description: The facility will channel an initial €40 million through local banks, with EU grants paid to firms after their projects are verified.

item.title: TOL Gases lists shares after raising 10.57bn/- in rights issue
item.description: The 129 per cent subscription will help fund a carbon dioxide plant and infrastructure expected to cost 15.7bn/-.

item.title: Sierra Leone passes 2027 MCC scorecard
item.description: The country met the benchmarks in an assessment of 104 nations, but passing does not guarantee it will receive development assistance.

item.title: Ruto returns to Parliament with Sh5 trillion plan under scrutiny
item.description: The National Infrastructure Fund holds Sh310.6 billion in starting capital, against a wider ambition to raise Sh5 trillion over a decade.

item.title: Nzovu links Lusaka-Ndola road progress to public-private partnerships
item.description: Zambia’s infrastructure minister made the case for private-sector partnerships while inspecting work on the 321-kilometre dual carriageway.

item.title: Zambia police reject clearance for two Lusaka term-limit marches
item.description: The planned processions, one for and one against removing presidential term limits, were set for November 25, 2026.

item.title: Zambia’s ECZ starts Mwinilunga review meetings on 2026 election
item.description: The Electoral Commission of Zambia began sessions with district structures to assess activities from the August 13 general election.

item.title: Fashion Sakala retires from Zambia’s international team
item.description: The Chipolopolo captain said representing Zambia and leading its national side were among the proudest moments of his life.

item.title: Malawi steps up gold purchases to fund fuel imports
item.description: Information Minister Shadric Namalomba says the government expects fuel supplies to improve, but cannot give a date for ending the crisis.

item.title: Tunis hosts six-day Italian-Tunisian arts festival in the medina
item.description: The programme runs through 21 November across cultural venues and schools, with most events free to attend.

item.title: Nigeria targets $9.3bn care economy and seeks private investment
item.description: The Federal Executive Council approved a 2026–2030 policy, while a proposed bill would give it legislative backing.

item.title: Bensouda pledges Banjul-Barra bridge before 2036 if elected
item.description: The Coalition 2026 presidential candidate says the link would strengthen trade and help make the North Bank Region The Gambia's commercial capital.

item.title: Guro opens 25 de Junho primary school and a supermarket
item.description: Mayor Latifo Vinho opened both facilities, with the school costing 5.8 million meticais to put up.

item.title: Thugge backs Treasury plan to centralise county deposits at CBK
item.description: The proposed law would require counties to get written Treasury approval before opening or closing accounts and move their funds into a single account.

item.title: Uganda's GROW project has lent Shs161 billion to women-owned businesses
item.description: The World Bank-backed programme has made 10,096 loans, with repayment terms of up to 24 months and interest capped at 10 per cent a year.

item.title: Cedi’s year-to-date fall against dollar reaches 10.6 per cent
item.description: Bank of Ghana data puts the dollar at GH¢11.69 on the interbank market in November, while Fitch Solutions forecasts further weakness in 2027.

item.title: Burkina Faso beat Mauritania 3-1 to qualify for CAN 2027
item.description: Aboubacar Camara, Franck Lassina Traoré and Elohim Kaboré scored in Nouakchott, securing qualification with two group matches left.

item.title: Liberia police reopen 2017 cheque complaint against Musa Hassan Bility
item.description: The opposition leader says his company’s cheque was never presented for payment and that the debt to former Nigerian partners was settled.

item.title: Coffee Quality Business buys Bukinanyana coffee and employs 110
item.description: Raphaël Yaminyibuka bought a local association and its coffee stock after returning to Burundi in 2023 with 25 million Burundian francs.

item.title: Seychelles opposition leader Bernard Georges calls 2027 budget a small-change plan
item.description: Georges said the budget made no major announcements and was a small-change plan, cutting into the spending response the government had promised.

item.title: FeRCAB opens Parakou production studio for 56 community radios
item.description: The shared facility, delivered with Fondation Hirondelle and European Union funding, is intended to help members produce radio and digital content.

item.title: COP31 draft sets $120 billion adaptation finance target for 2035
item.description: The proposed agreement also sets a 35 percent electricity target, while Liberia presses for predictable support and has undisbursed climate commitments.

item.title: Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi Movement takes US tour to seven states from November 21
item.description: The movement plans town halls, community dinners and meetings with elected officials, with Kenyan diaspora communities at the centre, until December 7.

item.title: Benin receives 81 million CFA francs in court equipment
item.description: The United States funded the equipment, while the United Nations Development Programme provided technical support for the justice project.

item.title: Malagasy jiu-jitsu athletes win three silver medals at Abu Dhabi worlds
item.description: Nofy Chuck, Ranaivomanana Idealisoa and Ranarivelo Ando Mahasoa finished second in their events at the Brazilian jiu-jitsu championship.

item.title: DA weighs mayoral swap as Johannesburg coalition talks stall
item.description: The proposal would send party leader Geordin Hill-Lewis to Johannesburg and Helen Zille to Cape Town, but Zille says she is not taking it seriously.

item.title: Liberia House committee urges rejection of OeSD ID concession
item.description: The lawmakers cite more than 40 alleged legal, procurement, financial and national-security defects in the proposed civil registry deal.

item.title: Namibia's EU exports rise more than 17% to N$17.6 billion
item.description: Exports to the bloc supported an estimated 40 000 direct jobs in 2025, a study presented in Windhoek found, with the EU now taking 19.4% of the country's total exports.

item.title: Ghana launches 2026-2028 migration strategy to coordinate agencies
item.description: Interior Minister Muntaka Mohammed Mubarak says the plan will strengthen migrant protection, border management and action against trafficking and smuggling.

item.title: EGENCO suspends William Liabunya over K2.6 billion payment
item.description: The board also suspended company secretary Videlia Mluwira as the state-owned power generator faces scrutiny over the payment.

item.title: Madagascar and US sign military logistics accord for maritime patrols
item.description: The deal lets both armed forces exchange supplies, services and logistical support for joint patrols, exercises and crisis response.

item.title: Ravinala Airports renovates Ivato terminal and adds passenger services
item.description: The airport operator has introduced free Wi-Fi, device-charging points and new rest areas at Madagascar’s national and international terminals.

item.title: Four Zimbabweans abandon bail bids in South Africa war-recruitment case
item.description: The fifth accused, Abel Muchenje, plans to seek release, but prosecutors told the Kempton Park court they will oppose his application.

item.title: Vibes on Main brings Mr JazziQ to Mbabane on 28 November
item.description: The South African DJ will lead the festival’s Phase One bill at Prince of Wales Stadium, alongside South African and Eswatini performers.

item.title: Eswatini inflation rises to 3.4 per cent ahead of CBE meeting
item.description: Annual inflation climbed from 2.9 per cent in September, ahead of the Central Bank's final Monetary Policy Consultative Committee meeting on Friday.

item.title: Eswatini brings in 104 grass bales for livestock farmers
item.description: The National Agricultural Marketing Board bought the feed in South Africa as farmers prepare for an anticipated El Niño drought.

item.title: Mali seal 2027 Africa Cup of Nations place with 2-0 win in Kigali
item.description: Goals from Modibo Sagnan and Gaoussou Diarra gave the Eagles a fourth straight qualifying victory and secured top spot in Group K.

item.title: Gambia lets 2-1 lead slip to draw with Ivory Coast
item.description: Musa Barrow scored a 79th-minute penalty, but Ivory Coast equalised with the final kick after Musa Badamosi was sent off.

item.title: Mauritania weighs border risks after UN ends MINURSO mandate
item.description: The Security Council declined to renew the Western Sahara mission on 30 October, removing a mechanism that monitored incidents and helped contain escalation.

item.title: ActionAid urges peaceful campaigning ahead of Gambia’s Dec. 5 vote
item.description: The non-partisan group called on candidates, parties and supporters to obey electoral laws and keep political competition free of intimidation and violence.

item.title: Soutra Money earns top-tier payment security certification
item.description: The Guinean fintech says its PCI DSS level 1 status follows a full audit and requires annual reviews of its payment systems and data safeguards.

item.title: CBG outlines alumina refinery plan at Conakry mining summit
item.description: The Guinean bauxite producer said construction work has begun and it expects to invite guests to a possible opening three years from next year.

item.title: Six teams qualify for 2027 Africa Cup of Nations
item.description: Mali, Burkina Faso, Benin, Cameroon and Morocco joined Senegal after Tuesday’s qualifying matches, with the final places still undecided.

item.title: Doumbouya appoints senior officials to Guinea’s labour ministry
item.description: A decree read on national television on 17 November names officials for employment, workplace safety and labour-market agencies.

item.title: Coris Foundation gives agricultural VDPs 360 tricycles
item.description: The 500 million FCFA donation is intended to help the volunteers travel to fields and move harvests to storage sites.

item.title: Burkina Faso trains 55 education workers in inclusive teaching and school safety
item.description: The four-day Ouagadougou course covers gender-sensitive teaching, preventing gender-based violence in schools and digital tools.

item.title: Burundi opposition parties name presidential candidates
item.description: The APDR filed Gabriel Banzawitonde’s bid without the full 100 million Burundian francs deposit, while the CNL chose Nestor Girukwishaka.

item.title: UCAD launches inclusion directorate and plans campus access work
item.description: The new office will assess community needs and oversee work on facilities for students with disabilities and psychological support.

item.title: Benin qualifies for 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after Burkina Faso win
item.description: Burkina Faso beat Mauritania 3-1 in Nouakchott on Tuesday, securing the Guépards a place without playing.

item.title: GETESA faces $432,270 debt to MTN over international roaming
item.description: Diario Rombe reports that the state telecom operator faces roaming cuts and possible court seizures over unpaid debt to the South African company.

item.title: Senegal arrests 26 in suspected irregular migration attempt at Abéné
item.description: The group included 24 Senegalese and two Gambians; investigators suspect two or three alleged organisers were posing as would-be migrants.

item.title: Cape Verde lose 2-0 to Liberia in 2027 Africa Cup qualifier
item.description: Liberia scored in the 47th and 86th minutes, leaving the Blue Sharks level with Liberia on three points in Group K.

item.title: Morocco and Mauritania move to update 1986 trade pact
item.description: The two governments also plan a framework for agricultural and food shipments and an investment forum in Mauritania in early 2027.

item.title: EMAE brings regular electricity to four communities in southern São Tomé
item.description: Four low-voltage transformer stations now provide round-the-clock public-grid power in Yo Grande, Dona Augusta, Praia Pesqueira and Ribeira Peixe.

item.title: Chadian professor elected secretary-general of francophone medical deans’ conference
item.description: Foumsou Lhagadang won the post in Bangui after an election process involving 19 countries, giving Chad a representative in the conference leadership.

item.title: GERD operations leave Sudan’s Roseires dam exposed to sudden flow changes
item.description: A study says releases from Ethiopia’s newly opened dam can alter levels at Sudan’s irrigation hub within hours, affecting water supplies and farms.

item.title: Comorian researcher Faïdat Mzé Hamadi defends doctoral thesis on legume foods in Nantes
item.description: Her thesis examined how the structure of legume-based model foods relates to their properties and the processes used to make them.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau beats Madagascar 2-0 to lead Group L with 10 points
item.description: Mauro Teixeira scored in the 69th minute in Bissau, giving the national side a three-point lead over second-placed Nigeria.
